title: feat(types): arm record:approvals and record:attachments from their spec rows (objectui#12363)
body:
Fixes #12363
Clause-②: yes

## What

`@objectstack/spec` 18 declares two page blocks, `record:approvals` and `record:attachments`. `@object-ui/app-shell` registers a renderer for each, and `buildDefaultPageSchema` (`@object-ui/plugin-detail`) emits both as the default record page's Approvals and Attachments tabs. But `AnyComponentSchema` had no arm for either. So `objectui validate` refused each one with `invalid_union` at `type`, and the record page objectui builds itself failed validation.

This PR reuses the construction of objectui#12342 (PR #12362, `52d6194`):

- **Arms (`@object-ui/types/zod`).** New module `zod/record-panels.zod.ts` with `RecordApprovalsBlockSchema` and `RecordAttachmentsBlockSchema`. Both are wired into `AnyComponentSchema`, so `StrictAnyComponentSchema` and `objectui validate` claim them too. Each `properties` bag restates its spec row. `body` / `children` are refused by name with `retirementTombstone`, as on #12342's arm.
- **TS twins (`@object-ui/types`).** New `record-panels.ts` with interfaces of the same two names, exported from the entry and added to `AnySchema`.
- **Mirror parity.** Two new pairs in `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`; `EXPECTED_MIRROR_PAIRS` goes 196 to 198. The emit-headroom member list in `any-component-emit-headroom-11573.test.ts` gains both arms.
- **Ratchet (`@object-ui/cli`).** `NAMESPACED_REFUSED_AT_TYPE` goes 308 to 306, lowered by exactly two. A new row names both keys as armed, with a control showing an unclaimed `record:` literal is still refused. The #12342 row's comment no longer says the siblings are unarmed.
- **Not in `public-blocks.zod.ts`.** That union is pinned to the ADR-0080 curated list, and neither block is curated, the same reason #12342 gave.
- Changeset: `.changeset/12363-approvals-attachments-arms.md`, `@object-ui/types` minor.

## Contract review: the accept set this widens (Clause-②)

**Installed spec.** `@objectstack/spec` `18.0.0-next.0`, as this checkout resolves it (`packages/types`). Both types are `PageComponentType` members, and both have a `ComponentPropsMap` row. This was measured at runtime and is re-read by the new test on every run.

| Type | Spec row | Row keys | Strict? | Arm `properties` | Accepted keys |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `record:approvals` | `RecordApprovalsProps` (not exported under that name from `@objectstack/spec/ui`) | none | yes (catchall never) | `z.strictObject({}).optional()` | none: only `{}` |
| `record:attachments` | `emptyProps('record:attachments')`, built inline and exported under no name | none | yes | `z.strictObject({}).optional()` | none: only `{}` |

Key by key: neither row declares a key, so neither bag declares one. ⛔ No key the spec does not declare, and no `passthrough` / `catchall`. Both rows are unnamed exports, so they cannot cross the objectui#8317 import boundary by reference. They are restated, which is `element:divider`'s and `record:approval_decision`'s situation.

`record-panels-arms-12363.test.ts` pins three things against the installed row on every run:
- the arm's bag key set equals the row's;
- the bag accepts or refuses five probe bags exactly as the row does;
- a CONTROL: the row itself accepts `{}` and refuses a key.

**What is refused:**
- Any key inside `properties` (`unrecognized_keys` at `properties`). This includes `approvals` and `currentUserId`. The spec's `RecordApprovalsProps` guidance names both as the HOST's runtime channel, "not authorable surface".
- A node-level `children` or `body`, refused by name (`invalid_type` at the key).
- A flat undeclared key, refused on the strict face (`unrecognized_keys`).

**What is accepted:** the bare node `{ type }`, and the node with `id` / `className` / an empty `properties` bag (the `BaseSchema` node keys).

**Published exports added:**
- `@object-ui/types/zod`: `RecordApprovalsBlockSchema`, `RecordAttachmentsBlockSchema`.
- `@object-ui/types`: the TS types of the same names, plus two new `AnySchema` members.
- `AnyComponentSchema` / `StrictAnyComponentSchema` gain two discriminator literals.

## Premise checks (dispatch section 2)

- **A1 holds.** Both are `PageComponentType` members with `ComponentPropsMap` rows on the installed spec. Both rows are strict and declare no key (table above).
- **A2 holds, with one boundary.** `buildDefaultPageSchema` emits `{ type: 'record:attachments' }` for an `enable.files: true` object, and `{ type: 'record:approvals' }` when the host passes `approvals`. That page now validates whole on both faces (pinned).
  - When the HOST also passes `approvals.node`, the synthesizer spreads it into the node's `properties`. `RecordDetailView` does this with its live `useRecordApprovals` read: `approvals` plus `currentUserId`. The arm refuses those two keys because the spec row does.
  - This is the same shape as `record:history`'s host `entries` / `loading`, which the existing arm already refuses.
  - The spec's own guidance describes that runtime path ("the default record page passes the approval requests it fetched through it at runtime"). That page is rendered through `SchemaRenderer` and never reaches the validator. So I read it as a host runtime channel, not a producer defect, and pinned it as a refusal. The arm is not widened for it. It is reported below.
- **A3 holds.** The ratchet is in `packages/cli/src/__tests__/registered-types-validate-ratchet-10859.test.ts`. It drops by exactly two, 308 to 306.
- **Serial note.** objectui#12370 (the next.1 bump) had not landed when this was pushed. `origin/main` moved by one commit, `fc211e817`, which touches neither `packages/types`, the lockfile nor the ratchet. So the rows are measured on next.0.

## Pins

- `packages/types/src/__tests__/record-panels-arms-12363.test.ts`. Per type, it pins:
  - the installed row is present and keyless, and the bag equals it;
  - the bare node validates on every face;
  - the type is claimed at `type`;
  - an undeclared key in the bag is refused;
  - a flat undeclared key is refused on the strict face;
  - `children` / `body` are refused by name;
  - the union reaches the arm itself.

  It also pins that `properties.approvals` / `properties.currentUserId` are refused.
- `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/buildDefaultPageSchema.validatesWhole-12363.test.ts`:
  - the default record page carries both panels, as a non-vacuity check;
  - it passes `safeValidateSchema` and `StrictAnyComponentSchema` with zero issues;
  - the Attachments-only page passes;
  - the host-payload page is refused with exactly one issue, `unrecognized_keys` at the `record:approvals` bag naming `approvals` and `currentUserId`.
- The cli ratchet row described above.

## Verification (head `83d91d3`)

- **vitest, full `packages/types/` and `packages/cli/`, plus the plugin-detail pin.** One run under the verify lock: `Test Files 409 passed (409)`, `Tests 10719 passed (10719)`. This includes `zod-mirror-parity`, `any-component-emit-headroom-11573`, `record-approval-decision-arm-12342` and the ratchet.
- **type-check.** `@object-ui/types`, `@object-ui/cli` and `@object-ui/plugin-detail` all exit 0. I built the dependency closure first.
- **Ablation** (`ablation-replace.mjs`, run with `--delete` on the two union members in `zod/index.zod.ts`):
  - anchor went 1 to 0, and the blob changed `cd2ce50` to `0f4b39f`;
  - the three pin files went red: `Test Files 3 failed (3)`, `Tests 24 failed | 50 passed (74)`;
  - the ratchet pin (`the refused count equals the pin`), the new ratchet row, all four default-page rows and every union-path arm row failed;
  - the bag-vs-row rows stayed green, as predicted, because they read the arm directly;
  - restore was proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.
- **Gates, each exit code read directly.** These all exit 0: `check:phantom-deps`, `self-import`, `unreferenced-sources`, `doc-example-readers`, `handler-key-reads`, `side-effects-array`, `element-data-source-declaration`, `spec-symbols`, `action-forward-parity`, `designer-field-key-parity`, `icon-record-names`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-drift`, `i18n-designer-parity`, `registry-bare-names`, `control-bytes` and `new-line-citations`. So do `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`.
- **`check:spec-floors` exits 1.** It says "The scan collapsed: 0 package(s) declare @objectstack/spec in a consumer-facing field". That is the known failure on `main` (objectui#12334), and this diff touches no dependency field.
- **Lint, narrowed.** `eslint --format json` over the 9 changed `.ts` files gives 9 results, 0 errors and 0 warnings, the way the package `lint` scripts run it (`eslint .` for types and plugin-detail, `eslint src` for cli).
  - With `--no-inline-config` it reports 3 findings, all on lines this diff does not touch: 2 in `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`, 1 in `types/src/index.ts`. Each is already covered by an inline disable.
  - `eslint.config.js` sets no `project` / `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware, and this diff cannot change the verdict on any untouched file.
  - The full `pnpm lint` run belongs to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **The file surface grew by one test file.** The dispatch named `packages/types/src/**`, the cli ratchet and their tests. The ruled pin "`buildDefaultPageSchema`'s page validates whole" cannot live in either package. `@object-ui/types` and `@object-ui/cli` do not depend on `@object-ui/plugin-detail`, and a reverse import is what `check:phantom-deps` refuses. So that pin is a new test file in `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/`, a package that already depends on `@object-ui/types`. No plugin-detail source changed.
- **The restated `record:approvals` bag drops the spec's guidance text.** The spec row's own unrecognized-key message explains why `approvals` and `currentUserId` are host channels. The restated `z.strictObject({})` reports only a generic `unrecognized_keys`. The arm's `.describe()` carries the same guidance for readers of the schema. Carrying the row's message would need the row by reference, which the objectui#8317 boundary census does not admit for an unnamed export.
- The arms do not spread `NODE_ENVELOPE` (`responsiveStyles`), as on #12342's and the `cloud:` arms. Neither block is offered by Studio, and no producer writes that key on these nodes.
